Utility Table of the U-BOIN Design

Source: R/uboin_utility_table.R
uboin_utility_table.Rd

Tabulate, for a dose with a given number of patients, the posterior mean utility and the admissibility of the dose for every possible number of responses, of DLTs and of responses without a DLT. These are the decision tables of the U-BOIN design of Zhou, Lee and Yuan (2019), which can be written into the protocol before the trial starts.

Usage

uboin_utility_table(
  n,
  tox_upper,
  resp_lower,
  utility = c(0, 30, 50, 100),
  cutoff_eli = 0.95,
  cutoff_eli_resp = 0.9,
  prior_tox = c(1, 1),
  prior_resp = c(1, 1)
)

Arguments

n

Integer scalar. Number of patients treated at the dose.

tox_upper

Numeric scalar. Highest acceptable DLT probability.

resp_lower

Numeric scalar. Lowest acceptable response probability.

utility

Numeric vector of length four. Utility of the outcomes (no response, DLT), (no response, no DLT), (response, DLT) and (response, no DLT). Defaults to c(0, 30, 50, 100).

cutoff_eli

Numeric scalar. Cutoff of the toxicity rule. Defaults to 0.95.

cutoff_eli_resp

Numeric scalar. Cutoff of the futility rule. Defaults to 0.90.

prior_tox

Numeric vector of length two. Beta prior of the toxicity rule. Defaults to c(1, 1).

prior_resp

Numeric vector of length two. Beta prior of the futility rule. Defaults to c(1, 1).

Value

A data frame with one row per possible outcome of the n patients and columns

n_resp

Number of responses.

n_tox

Number of DLTs.

n_resp_no_tox

Number of responses without a DLT.

utility

Posterior mean utility of the dose.

toxic

Whether the dose is toxic.

futile

Whether the dose is futile.

admissible

Whether the dose is neither toxic nor futile.

Details

The posterior mean utility is sum(utility * (1/4 + n_k)) / (1 + n), with n_k the patients with each outcome, as in uboin_simulate. A dose is toxic when the posterior probability that its DLT probability exceeds tox_upper is above cutoff_eli, and futile when the posterior probability that its response probability is below resp_lower is above cutoff_eli_resp.

Tables S4 to S6 of the supporting information of the article, for 3, 6 and 9 patients and the utilities c(0, 15, 25, 100), are reproduced with prior_resp = c(0.05, 0.05); with the default Beta(1, 1) prior a dose without any response among 3, 6 or 9 patients is admissible, whereas those tables mark it inadmissible.

References

Zhou, Y., Lee, J. J. and Yuan, Y. (2019). A utility-based Bayesian optimal interval (U-BOIN) phase I/II design to identify the optimal biological dose for targeted and immune therapies. Statistics in Medicine, 38(28), S5299-S5316. doi:10.1002/sim.8361

See also

uboin_simulate, uboin_select_obd

Examples

# Table S4 of the supporting information of the article
tab <- uboin_utility_table(3, tox_upper = 0.30, resp_lower = 0.20,
                           utility = c(0, 15, 25, 100),
                           prior_resp = c(0.05, 0.05))
tab[tab$admissible, ]
#>    n_resp n_tox n_resp_no_tox utility toxic futile admissible
#> 5       1     0             1   41.25 FALSE  FALSE       TRUE
#> 6       1     1             0   22.50 FALSE  FALSE       TRUE
#> 7       1     1             1   37.50 FALSE  FALSE       TRUE
#> 8       1     2             0   18.75 FALSE  FALSE       TRUE
#> 9       1     2             1   33.75 FALSE  FALSE       TRUE
#> 11      2     0             2   62.50 FALSE  FALSE       TRUE
#> 12      2     1             1   43.75 FALSE  FALSE       TRUE
#> 13      2     1             2   58.75 FALSE  FALSE       TRUE
#> 14      2     2             0   25.00 FALSE  FALSE       TRUE
#> 15      2     2             1   40.00 FALSE  FALSE       TRUE
#> 17      3     0             3   83.75 FALSE  FALSE       TRUE
#> 18      3     1             2   65.00 FALSE  FALSE       TRUE
#> 19      3     2             1   46.25 FALSE  FALSE       TRUE
